entries.rationale: Public sitemaps API parameter that genuinely propagates into the outbound urlopen URL, but only as the urlencode'd 'sitemap' query-string value on the ping URL: ping_google() -> _get_sitemap_full_url(sitemap_url) -> params = urlencode({'sitemap': sitemap_full_url}) -> urlopen('%s?%s' % (ping_url, params)). Host/scheme/port of the request are NOT controllable through this parameter (they come from ping_url, whose in-tree value is the fixed constant PING_URL). Sole in-tree caller is the ping_google management command (CLI positional arg, operator-controlled). Kept as candidate for human review: propagation is real, attacker control is weak (CLI operator, query-string position only).

entries.rationale: Host/scheme-controlling input of the fetch: urlopen('%s?%s' % (ping_url, params)) takes ping_url as the prefix of the requested URL, so a caller-supplied ping_url fully controls scheme/host/port/path of the server-side request. No scheme/host validation exists at the call site and urlopen's default opener follows redirects. However, no in-tree caller passes ping_url - it defaults to the fixed PING_URL constant 'https://www.google.com/webmasters/tools/ping' and the only in-tree caller (the ping_google management command) never sets it, so no attacker-controlled fetch exists in this codebase. Candidate (library-API surface for out-of-tree application callers); requires human review.
